messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Conway–Maxwell–Poisson distribution
parts:
Ben's been wanting to look at some of these more general
distributions.

I don't think we have that Z function used to normalize
the pmf:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conwayï¿½Maxwellï¿½Poisson_distribution

If someone wanted to implement the Z function it'd be easy
enough to specify the pmf in Stan. (For all I know it can be implemented
out of pieces we have.)

Even better, someone could build a vectorized form of the distribution that
used the Z function, and then the GLM model would be trivial to code for
any link function.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Conway–Maxwell–Poisson distribution
parts:
We can't use R code directly for two reasons: (1) we need
functions to be templated independently on all the arguments
that can be parameters (preferably all non-int parameters);
(2) the licenses are not compatible, and due to licensing issues.

Our example distributions are all very complicated because they're
all vectorized. But if you don't care about the speed boost
of vectorization, you can just implement it for single arguments
following the way any other function in Stan is implemented.
For instance, look at binomial_coefficient_log() or atan2(),
which are binary functions and a lot simpler than looking
at the probability functions.

You should also look at the following for instructions on how
to make the function visible to the Stan modeling language:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Contributing-New-Functions-to-Stan

In order to get something into Stan itself, we require unit tests
and documentation and bounds checks on the function. We can help with
that if you don't have time to do it, but no promises on when we'll
get to it.

- Bob
